title: Karol G’s ‘BbY WOW’ Lyrics & English Translation: What Song Does It Sample? - Just Jared
content: The 35-year-old Colombian superstar’s “BbY WOW” with Judeline and Rusowsky, featured on her new album NO ME ARREPIENTO DE SENTIR TANTO, is steadily surging up the streaming charts, and fans are eagerly looking up the lyrics and English translation, as well as the familiar song it samples. As of the end of August, the song broke through the Billboard Hot 100 to No. 38, and is already a No. 1 hit on US Hot Latin Songs and Hot Latin Rhythm Songs charts. Karol broke down the story behind the song in an in-depth interview for Rolling Stone. I felt like I needed a song, one that people could dance to in the club but that also had that emotion. So, what happens when you’re in the club and you’re heartbroken? You just think about the other person, about the song you’d love to be dancing to with that person. The first version of the song was just me. But I felt like, live, I wanted to sing that song with more people on stage and for it to really become a bit more of a party. And that’s when I thought of Rusowsky and I said to Judeline, “Why don’t you join the song?” I worked a lot on that album with Judeline because the way she sings about love made me feel how men sometimes don’t understand how deep a woman’s pain can be. She has something special, and it’s that every emotion feels so intense. She has a song called “Is God Good or Just Powerful?” It’s literally one that lasts about a minute and a half. What she sings is super short, it’s like a verse and a chorus. And I was like, “Wow, how can you say so much in a verse and a chorus?” So it was literally a must for me to write music with her for this album. Our teams got in touch. We told her I was making new music and she traveled to Los Angeles. I spent about a week with her, and it was really nice because the first thing we did was sit down and talk, like, “I’ll give you some context about where I am, how I’m feeling.”We were both going through almost the same thing, so I loved that because we were in sync and it just worked. I thought, “We’re both here, feeling almost the same thing, it’s going to flow in a special way.”We were in the studio for about three or four days, and we made more music there that isn’t on the album. The song samples the “Coolie Dance” riddim by Cordell ‘Scatta’ Burrell and Everton, as popularized on “Move Ya Body,” the 2004 hit by Nina Sky featuring Jabba and Kat DeLuna‘s “Whine Up,” among other hits over the years. Kehlani also used it on 2024’s “After Hours.” Posted To:Cordell Burrell Jabba Judeline Karol G Music Nina Sky No Me Arrepiento De Sentir Tanto Rusowsky We won't sell or share your personal information to inform the ads you see. title: The Corner Office teaser: Why G.S. Ramesh tried to create a ‘Hindian’ culture at Hyundai - HR Katha
content: When G.S. Ramesh joined Hyundai as its first Indian employee, he found himself at the intersection of two very different approaches to work. The Korean management culture brought its own expectations around discipline, performance and ways of working. The Indian workforce brought a different cultural context. For Ramesh, the challenge was not to turn one into the other. “You cannot convert Indians to Koreans. And you cannot become Indian. So better synergise yourself,” he recalls in a conversation with HRKatha. His response was to think about a culture that could draw from both. He even coined a word for it: “Hindian” — Hyundai plus Indian. The experience offers a glimpse into a much longer professional journey. Ramesh began his career with Tata before becoming Hyundai’s first Indian employee and, eventually, an entrepreneur himself. In the upcoming episode of The Corner Office by HRKatha, G.S. Ramesh, Founder & Chairman, Layam Group, joins Prajjal Saha, Founder & Editor, HRKatha, for a conversation about the experiences, organisations and choices that shaped the entrepreneur he eventually became. The discussion travels across nearly five decades, from his early corporate years to building Layam Group, but also explores a larger question: what do leaders carry from the cultures they have worked in when they eventually set out to build one of their own? title: Vikings Mourn Death of Former QB & Punter Bob Lee - Minnesota Vikings
content:
EAGAN, Minn. — The Vikings are mourning the loss of former quarterback and punter Bob Lee, who passed away Aug. 17, just 10 days after he turned 81. Lee holds the distinction of punting in Minnesota's first Super Bowl appearance (IV) and throwing the most recent touchdown by a Viking in a Super Bowl (XI), a 13-yarder caught by Stu Voigt in the fourth quarter against the Raiders. He made the Vikings roster in 1969 and played in the NFL through 1980, totaling 77 regular-season games played for Minnesota, Atlanta and the Los Angeles Rams. In 30 starts at quarterback, Lee posted a 19-11 record with the Vikings. He played in eight postseason games, making three starts. That's pretty impressive, considering he entered the NFL as a 17th-round pick (441st overall out of 462 picks) out of the University of the Pacific in 1968. Lee made his pro debut in the 1969 season opener, punting six times in a game at the Giants in which Fran Tarkenton led New York to a comeback win against his previous and future team. The following week, after Joe Kapp tied an NFL record with seven touchdown passes against the Baltimore Colts, Lee attempted his first pro passes, going 4-for-6 with 35 yards in the 52-14 Vikings win. Lee first met Kapp (with Vikings 1967-69) long before they became teammates. In fall 2019 both were among attendees during a 50th anniversary celebration of the 1969 NFL Champions. The reunion included panel discussions, during which Lee shared his memory of meeting Kapp the first time when Kapp was QB at Cal and Lee was 12. "I met Joe Kapp when I was 12 years old and he was a junior at the University of California on a 1-9 team," Lee explained. "My dad ran The Associated Press in San Francisco. They were in competition with other wire services. They hired a college senior journalism student to do the postgame stories. Those stories for the Eastern papers paid a nickel a word. They were 1,500 words, so 75 bucks, which was a big deal in 1957. "The senior didn't show up. They said, 'The press pass works. Go down there, write a bunch of notes. We'll turn it into a story.' The first guy I listened to was Joe Kapp," Lee continued. "Joe took all the blame for the loss. Nobody else. It was his fault. … He was a leader. He didn't push himself in certain directions on other people." Lee attempted one pass in a 51-3 win over Cleveland on Nov. 9, 1969, and went 3-for-4 with his first touchdown, a 7-yard strike to John Henderson in a 52-14 win over the Steelers two weeks later. During the 1969 postseason, Lee punted three times in a 23-20 win over the Rams and thrice more in a 27-7 victory over the Browns, helping Minnesota advance to Super Bowl IV. He punted three times in that game as well. After making two starts as a backup late in 1970 but not punting that season, he returned to those duties in 1971. Lee made four starts in the regular season, as well as the playoff game against Dallas in the Divisional Round. Lee also handled punting duties in that loss to the Cowboys. That was the final time he punted in an NFL game. Tarkenton's return to Minnesota in 1972 led to Lee returning to a reserve QB role before he was traded to Atlanta in 1973, when he posted his best results, going 8-2 for the Falcons. After one more season there, he returned to Minnesota in 1975. Lee backed up Tarkenton over the next four seasons and went 4-1 in five starts from 1976-77. "Bob Lee was under appreciated at how good he was at quarterback," Tarkenton said. "He was a great backup QB for us and a good starter for the Atlanta Falcons. Plus, Bob was an absolutely great human being that you could depend on anytime. He was as good of a teammate as you could ever have." When Tarkenton suffered a broken leg in mid-November of the 1977 season, Lee won three of four starts to help Minnesota finish 9-5. Playing through a broken right hand during the stretch, he then quarterbacked the Vikings to a win over the Rams in the Divisional Round of the NFC Playoffs, a game that came to be known as the "Mud Bowl." "Playing on a field like this is worse than snow," Lee said after the game. "You're slipping, your runners are slipping and your receivers are slipping. I think the thing that I was most impressed by was the way our ball carriers and receivers held onto the ball. It's kind of amazing that we didn't have one turnover." Rams QB Pat Haden threw interceptions to Nate Allen, Paul Krause and Jeff Wright. The Cowboys, however, prevailed over the Vikings in the NFC Championship Game on the way to a convincing win in Super Bowl XII. Lee capped his career with two seasons as a backup with the Rams. His final scoring pass was a 41-yarder against the Vikings in a pivotal 27-21 overtime win for L.A. From 1991-96 Lee proudly served as director of athletics at University of the Pacific, helping expand the school's athletics and fitness facilities. He became one of 22 charter members in the Pacific Athletics Hall of Fame in 1982. Other roles Lee held including serving on the board of directors for the Northern California chapter of the National Football Foundation and Hall of Fame, as well as chairman of the San Francisco Special Olympics in 1981. © 2026 Minnesota Vikings Football, LLC , All Rights Reserved. title: BMW R 1300 GS: The Adventure Bike That Eliminates The Need For A Second Motorcycle - Top Speed
content: Subscribe to the TopSpeed newsletter to never miss an update Owning multiple motorcycles sounds like the dream. You have one for weekday commuting, another for weekend canyon roads, and a third to disappear into the wilderness. Reality, however, slaps you in the face and reminds you that more motorcycles mean higher insurance costs, more maintenance, and more garage space. That's why many riders don't look for a bike that satisfies just one purpose, but one that handles a wide variety of rides. Motorcycles capable of handling nearly every situation have become more desirable over the years, and adventure bikes are leading that charge. A one-bike garage is simple. You don’t divide riding time between specialized machines. Instead, with every passing mile, you build familiarity with a single motorcycle. You learn its strengths, understand its personality, and develop your confidence in your skills, regardless of whether the road ahead looks freshly paved or covered in loose gravel. Adventure motorcycles have become the biggest reason why single-bike ownership is a realistic option. They combine upright ergonomics, long-travel suspension, generous luggage options, and capable engines, allowing riders to travel wherever they choose, be it their workplace or a remote village few others have visited. ADVs have steadily evolved into some of the most versatile machines on the market. While early generations leaned heavily toward either off-road exploration or long-distance touring, today’s flagship bikes are engineered to do both exceptionally well. They get large fuel capacities, advanced electronics, adaptive suspension, sophisticated rider aids, and increasingly refined engines. Riders today don't even have to choose between highway comfort and off-road capability, because most modern ADVs are designed to deliver both in the same package. Now, if you are looking for something that balances everything perfectly, there is exactly one bike for it. Need to commute? The bike feels manageable despite its size. Planning a thousand-mile road trip? This is built for exactly that. Curious about what’s at the end of a dirt track? Long-travel suspension and enduro equipment to the rescue. For decades, the BMW GS family has become the benchmark against which nearly every large ADV is measured. The R 1300 GS continues that legacy while introducing one of the most comprehensive redesigns the model has ever received. Compared with the previous R 1250 GS, almost every major component has been reworked. There is a new steel sheet-metal main frame, a die-cast aluminum rear frame, a more compact boxer engine, lower overall weight, updated suspension, and significantly expanded electronic capabilities. BMW also focused heavily on improving everyday usability. The lower center of gravity thanks to the boxer engine contributes to low-speed balance, while an optional automated transmission and adaptive ride height reduce intimidation for shorter riders. The result is an adventure bike that appeals equally to world travelers and daily commuters alike. At the heart of the BMW R 1300 GS sits a 1,300 cc air/liquid-cooled flat twin engine (best known as a boxer twin) that churns out 145 horsepower at 7,750 rpm and 110 pound-feet of torque at 6,500 rpm. This makes it one of the most powerful production boxer engines BMW has ever installed in one of its motorcycles. The best part? Despite the increased output and capacity, the engine is actually more compact than before. BMW repositioned the transmission beneath the engine while redesigning the overall layout to save space and reduce weight. Now, the engine’s personality changes dramatically depending on how the motorcycle is configured. Power delivery is broad, but the ride modes allow the rider to adjust throttle response and traction to their particular use case. There is an ECO mode that incorporates BMW's ShiftCam technology. This varies valve timing and valve lift to improve fuel economy as well as power delivery on long stretches of highway. The R 1300 GS also comes with a six-speed gearbox as standard. However, optionally, you can ask for the Automated Shift Assistant. This allows for fully automatic shifting or manual operation without a conventional clutch lever. A welcome feature when you consider what a burden stop-and-go traffic can be on the daily commute. The R 1300 GS represents one of the most comprehensive redesigns in the model's history. BMW replaced the tubular steel frame with an entirely new steel sheet-metal main frame for increased rigidity and tighter packaging size. The rear, too, has a new die-cast aluminum lattice rear frame. This is suspended on BMW's signature EVO Telelever front suspension and EVO Paralever rear suspension, while braking is handled by two 310 mm discs at the front with four-piston radial calipers, and a single 285 mm disc at the rear clamped by a two-piston floating caliper. Now, suspension technology has become one of the biggest advantages of premium adventure motorcycles, and the R 1300 GS pushes that even further. BMW’s Dynamic Suspension Adjustment continuously adapts damping characteristics according to riding conditions, throttle inputs, speed, and road surface. This is optional, but combined with the adaptive vehicle height features, it makes low-speed maneuvers, starts and stops, and parking considerably easier, even with a full load of luggage strapped to the bike. Although completely redesigned, the BMW R 1300 GS remains instantly recognizable as a GS. The signature boxer engine continues to define its silhouette, and the bodywork is noticeably more compact, improving both balance and reach to the ground. Ergonomics place the rider in a commanding upright position, giving them excellent control and reduced fatigue during long journeys. You also get multiple seat heights, adjustable ergonomics, luggage systems, and comfort packages to tailor the bike for touring, off-road expeditions, or even everyday riding. The R 1300 GS showcases just how sophisticated adventure motorcycles have become. A full-color TFT display provides navigation, smartphone connectivity, riding data, and vehicle information. LED lighting comes standard, while an optional adaptive headlight actively follows the motorcycle through corners. Radar-based Riding Assistant tech introduces active cruise control, front collision warning, lane change warning, and rear-end collision warning. Keyless ride, heated grips, tire pressure monitoring, hill start control, engine drag torque control, and numerous other electronic rider aids round out an already extensive suite of technology.​​​​​​​ Replacing multiple motorcycles is an ambitious goal, but the BMW R 1300 GS comes remarkably close. It possesses enough comfort for long-distance touring, enough performance to satisfy spirited road riding, enough capability for genuine off-road exploration, and enough practicality to function as everyday transportation. The search for the perfect all-around motorcycle has always been difficult, but the GS blends those qualities more effectively than most of its rivals. We want to hear from you. title: Vikings at Broncos Game Observations - Minnesota Vikings
content:
DENVER — The Vikings preseason wrapped Friday night with Carson Wentz starting at quarterback and playing two series before handing the reins of Minnesota's offense to Max Brosmer. Minnesota Head Coach Kevin O'Connell and Denver Head Coach Sean Payton opted to rest starters on both sides of the ball in the 34-6 Broncos win. O'Connell had hoped J.J. McCarthy was able to recover from an ankle injury suffered on a hit the previous week against the Baltimore Ravens. McCarthy was limited in practice early in the week and did not participate at all Wednesday in a practice that had more of a scrimmage format. Wentz finished 3-for-4 passing with 15 yards and a passer rating of 80.2. His longest completion was a gain of 6 to tight end Gavin Bartholomew. Brosmer opened by hitting his first few short completions and drove the Vikings 55-yards into the red zone late in the second quarter before the drive stalled in the red zone. Will Reichard booted a 28-yard field goal to cap the drive that lasted 4:00. The only problem was Denver stormed right back by driving 65 yards in just 1:08 thanks to Sam Ehlinger going 4-for-5 and accounting for all 65 yards through the air. Jaleel McLaughlin capped the drive with a 20-yard catch-and-run touchdown, securing the grab on the right side and showing his speed as he zoomed to the left. Brosmer finished 20-of-35 passing with 166 yards and a passer rating of 69.5 Ehlinger finished 15-for-20 with 233 yards and three scores. His passer rating was 131.9. View game action photos from the Vikings preseason game vs. the Broncos at Empower Field at Mile High. Undrafted rookie Jacob Thomas had really been making the most of his opportunities and started on Friday along with third-round pick Jakobe Thomas, who made his pro debut after missing Minnesota's first two preseason contests because of back tightness. Jacob Thomas unfortunately suffered an injury while defending a pass on the seventh play of the game. He was slow to get up after landing out of bounds. It was a tough end to a preseason that had started with such promise for Thomas, who recorded an interception at New York in his NFL debut. Jacob Thomas was replaced by Kahlef Hailassie, who recorded an interception in the second quarter to set up Minnesota's first score. Linebacker Jacob Roberts, who had recorded Minnesota's other interception against the Giants, also left the game with an injury. One of the battles that hadn't yielded much indication is at punter where veteran Johnny Hekker and undrafted rookie Brett Thorson. It likely wasn't going to be decided by Friday's action alone, which is good because the stats were about as even as possible. Thorson punted three times for 156 yards for an average of 52.0 and with a long of 58. Hekker? Three punts for 156 yards and an average of 52.0 with a long of 57. Times inside the 20-yard line? Twice each for both players. Ehlinger enjoyed a fourth quarter for the ages. He was able to orchestrate a 17-play 85 yard drive that lasted 9:58 and concluded with a 14-yard touchdown pass to Cody Schrader on fourth-and-2 with 13:04 remaining. Ehlinger also capitalized on a busted coverage that left rookie tight end Justin Joly completely uncovered in the middle of the field. Joly was able to catch it and run for an 88-yard score to cap a 93-yard drive that lasted just three plays and 1:39. The Broncos racked up 412 yards by going 7-for-14 on third downs and averaged 6.4 yards per play. Denver went 2-for-3 on fourth downs. Minnesota was unable to push the ball down the field much and finished with 270 yards. The Vikings went 3-for-13 on third downs and averaged 4.7 yards per play. The Vikings concluded the season with just one touchdown across three games (a fade from Wentz to Myles Price at New York). Minnesota went 0-for-2 on trips inside Denver's 20-yard line. title: Gold Is Forecast to Climb as Central Banks Buy the Precious Metal - Goldman Sachs
content: We harness every resource, insight, relationship, and competitive advantage to drive superior results for our clients. Gold is projected to extend its recent gains in the second half of 2026, even as growing use of some derivatives tied to the metal could be making gold prices more volatile, according to Goldman Sachs Research. Goldman Sachs Research forecasts the precious metal will rise to $4,900 per troy ounce by the end of the year. Gold rallied 15% from its mid-July low to around $4,600 per troy ounce as of August 25. The metal is expected to rise as central banks continue diversifying their reserves and markets scale back expectations for US rate hikes in 2026. Demand for gold from central banks is a key structural factor underpinning the metal’s rally, according to Lina Thomas, senior commodities analyst in Goldman Sachs Research, and Daan Struyven, co-head of Global Commodities Research. “We continue to see elevated central bank gold accumulation as a multi-year trend, as central banks diversify their reserves to hedge geopolitical and financial risks, consistent with recent survey evidence,” Thomas and Struyven write. Central banks have been diversifying their holdings using gold, which is considered less likely to be frozen than reserves held in foreign currencies. They have been buying gold at an increased rate since 2022, when G7 countries responded to the invasion of Ukraine by freezing Russian central bank assets in Europe. Goldman Sachs Research expects central banks to buy an average of 50 tonnes of gold per month in 2026, up from an average of 17 tonnes per month before 2022. Central bank purchases accelerated to 100 tonnes per month in June 2026 (on a three-month seasonally adjusted basis) from 66 tonnes the previous month, according to Goldman Sachs Research’s nowcast of central bank activity. China’s central bank was the largest identifiable buyer in the market in June. Interest rate expectations are another important factor supporting recent gold price increases. Demand from some investors is starting to recover from a slow first half of the year as markets scale back expectations of a Federal Reserve rate hike in 2026. Historically, gold tends to struggle when interest rates rise, as higher rates reduce the appeal of gold relative to yielding assets like bonds. “We expect the Fed-related headwind to abate further, as our economists expect a lower inflation trend to keep the Fed on hold this year,” Thomas and Struyven write. The researchers also highlight a range of medium-term factors that could cause the gold price to exceed Goldman Sachs Research’s forecast for 2026. “Gold’s share in private portfolios remains low, and recent geopolitical developments—including Iran and broader tensions—may accelerate diversification beyond central banks to private investors, including by weighing on perceptions of Western fiscal sustainability.” Demand for gold call options is rising as investors turn to the instruments to hedge their portfolios against large-scale changes in government policies. This has the potential to amplify price swings in both directions, Thomas and Struyven explain. As gold rises, it is approaching key strike levels for some call options, forcing options dealers that sold these calls to buy gold in order to hedge their short exposure to the metal, accelerating the rally. On the other hand, declines in the gold price could prompt dealers to reverse those hedges by selling their gold holdings, driving prices even lower. Goldman Sachs Research’s forecast for gold to reach $4,900 per troy ounce by the end of 2026 does not incorporate elevated demand for hedges through gold derivatives. This could increase the likelihood that the gold price exceeds the forecast, but it also suggests “greater two-sided volatility” to the gold rally, Thomas and Struyven write. title: What Is the Outlook for Diesel and Gasoline Supplies? - Goldman Sachs

Energy markets have been surprisingly resilient amid the disruption to shipping through the Strait of Hormuz. However, there are few signs of relief in markets for refined products such as diesel, gasoline, and jet fuel, says Nitin Jindal, head of Global Commodities in Goldman Sachs FICC and Equities, on The Markets podcast. Jindal also discusses China’s remarkable adjustment to the disruption in energy supplies and the outlook for natural gas prices in Europe as winter approaches. Chris Hussey: This is The Markets. I'm Chris Hussey, and today is Wednesday, August 26th, and we're here on the Goldman Sachs trading floor with Nitin Jindal, who heads up our global commodities business within global banking and markets. Nitin, thanks so much for joining us on The Markets. Chris Hussey: Okay. I want to start with a breaking point question because we're about to celebrate, celebrate is not the right word, the sixth straight month of the Strait of Hormuz being closed. Has it surprised you that this has not disrupted the commodity markets more, or do you think we really are at a breaking point? Nitin Jindal: Several things have surprised me, right? First, just the length of the war. That's surprising. But it shouldn't be surprising given what is happening in Europe, where we have-- we are at a four-and-a-half-year point, and nobody would have ever predicted at any point that that conflict would go this long. The other thing which is very surprising is how resilient the market has been in terms of finding supplies and not actually breaking down. Nitin Jindal: There are several things which have- which were done, several protective measures which were taken. Still, have a major, epically major disruption in the market, and prices are, you know, within a tolerable range. Chris Hussey: Okay, let me explore this one element around inventories. Cause some of the pictures I've been seeing lately is oil inventories are coming down now, and they're down to levels where we haven't seen them normally. Does that get you concerned that we're going into a place where we just have no more oil to give back and we're finally going to get that breaking point? Nitin Jindal: If you'd have asked me that question two months ago, my answer would have been absolutely yes. We were heading into the highest demand window, which is typically summer. Now we are kind of getting out of the demand window, and we were fine in the summer window. So especially for crude oil, I don't think we'll break in next few months. Products might be a different story. We have a very tight products market. The refining complex stays tight. We are getting less product out of Persian Gulf. We're getting less product out of Russia due to attacks on Russian refining by Ukraine. We're not getting products out of China due to just preservation. So the world ex-Persian Gulf, ex-Russia, ex-China is tight products, and there is no immediate release valve which is coming. Having said that, prices are already high, so what we like is we like the roll-up, which exists in the market, specially in crack spread space. Chris Hussey: Let me explore China for a little bit, if we can, because China has been an area which has had some demand destruction to help out with everything that's taking place. Can we see any more demand destruction out of China, or is that all we got? Nitin Jindal: It's highly unpredictable. Six months ago, nobody could have predicted that China could adjust by that, that much amount. But now that we, we have seen it, let's look at the hard data which makes it happen. China sells 34 million cars a year right now, so their fleet is growing rapidly, but a lot of it is EV. They can, hence they can switch from gas to electric easy. Their electricity sector is also growing rapidly. Last year, they installed 500 gigawatts of new capacity, mostly solar, some wind, some batteries, some gas. To put it in perspective, US only installed 50 gigs. And hence, they have no shortage of electricity. They can easily switch if needed without using more hydrocarbons. I would be surprised they can do a lot more, but I would also not be shocked if they did more Chris Hussey: Okay. So, one last commodity I wanted to talk about was nat gas, because there's a commodity that's more to do with Europe maybe than China, but China needs nat gas. If they can't get it from the Middle East, they might take it from the US, and then not enough gets to Europe. How much trouble will Europe get in if the Strait of Hormuz isn't reopened here and they can't get the LNG out to the right spots? Nitin Jindal: In the short term, it really depends on what happens this winter weather, right? Like, you must have also heard this term El Niño. El Niños are warm. So if you have a warm, if you have this El Niño which turns out to be very warm, you know, the world is going to get bailed out because the swing in gas demand due to weather is so strong that you can easily manage the supply disruption. And if you go past this season, there was so much oversupply coming from like US, Australia, that you could see a balanced market. Now, that's only true if you get a very, very warm winter. If you get a normal winter, you have a very tight setup going into this winter. If you get a normal winter, China will literally need to back off because Europe would then compete. And Europe would not just compete for gas. Europe would compete for gas and coal. Both very important fuels for China. Now, the flip side to that is that China itself produces about 30 BCF a day of natural gas. They have been growing their production. So, if you look at last year or so, China has stopped taking more LNG than what they used to historically take. Can they actually adjust that down by 20%? Probably, but that's not enough to offset the supply loss we have from Qatar. Chris Hussey: Yeah, I guess the ironic good news here is there's a super El Niño taking place here, which suggests normal weather might be less likely than normal. Chris Hussey: Okay. Put a bow on all this. What's the trade? Nitin Jindal: We like being long crack spreads, right? Specifically, term like Cal 27 cracks are not, you know, pricing continued disruption. We like being long Asian hydrocarbons versus US hydrocarbons. We think the freight market is tight. It will continue to stay tight. Look, if you look at, you know, Panama Canal is very tight right now. You cannot simply relieve all these supply chain logistics quickly. So, but when you again look at the forward freight market, it's not fully pricing all these dislocations. We like gold as a debasement trade. We like US nat gas as well going into this winter. Again, assuming normal-ish winter. So those are big themes like. We like US power market on the AI theme. Chris Hussey: Okay. What are you looking for in the, uh, couple of weeks ahead here? Nitin Jindal: You know, bring the summer to an end. Looking back, for kids to go to school. And I have a trip coming up in Europe next month. Chris Hussey: All right, great. And hopefully, in the middle of all that, you'll be able to watch a little cricket and see if India can beat Sri Lanka. Nitin Jindal: Well, I'll let you know tomorrow. Thank you so much. Chris Hussey: Thanks so much. That does it for this week's episode of The Markets. I'm Chris Hussey. Thanks for listening. title: Karol G’s Complicated and Relatable Heartbreak Brought Her Back to the Top of the Charts (Critic’s Take) - Billboard
content:
Here's why the Colombian star's 'No Me Arrepiento de Sentir Tanto' ended Bad Bunny's run at No. 1 on Top Latin Albums. It took a whole lot of heartache to bump Bad Bunny’s Debí Tirar Más Fotos and its title track off the No. 1 spots on Billboard’s Top Latin Albums and Hot Latin Songs chart. But Karol G did it. Not with hardcore perreo or the female empowerment anthems that have become her trademark, but with the vulnerability of a broken heart. Karol G’s No Me Arrepiento de Sentir Tanto (I’m Not Sorry for Feeling So Much) debuted at No. 1 on Billboard’s Top Latin Albums chart (dated Aug. 22), putting an end to Bad Bunny’s reign on top with Debí Tirar Más Fotos, which hadn’t moved from the top spot since Jan. 24. All told, that album has spent a record 77 nonconsecutive weeks atop the chart, and could easily claim that spot again. Not this week, though: Karol G’s Me Arrepiento holds firm at No. 1 for a second week (on the Billboard 200, the album dropped from No. 8 to No. 11). And on top of that, the Colombian star has also continued to hold “DtMF” from the top spot on Hot Latin Songs. There, Karol G claimed the top spot last week with “Ahí,” featuring Drake, and this week, she did it again with a different song — “Bby WOW” — featuring two Spanish up and comers: singer-songwriter Judeline and producer-keyboardist rusowsky. It takes a lot to move Bad Bunny from any position of dominance. That Karol has managed to do so with unconventional pairings and unconventional music (for her) says a lot about the rarified position she’s carved for herself in today’s pop music landscape, able to traverse genres and moods and still hold fast to her fans. Her feat also highlights how those fans are willing and able to move from the heavy-handed reggaetón beat that long dominated the charts to more sophisticated and understated fare, underscoring that Latin music tastes have decidedly evolved over the years, regardless of what new music playlists decide to include. Bad Bunny also made a big change to his sound with his Fotos album. But while Bad Bunny delved back into his roots for his acclaimed blockbutser, Karol G went more into a universal pop/dance/alt mood, and the two tracks from her new set that have topped Hot Latin Songs offer glimmers of mid-tempo rhythm on an album where melancholy dominates, awash in different sonic ambiences. Karol G thrives musically on heartache. Her best songs have long been rooted in failed relationships — their aftermath and then, their redemption — going back as far as 2017’s melancholic “A Ella,” dedicated to the woman who stole her man. But here, nearly a decade later, she’s amped up her message. She’s devastated rather than angry; her loneliness doesn’t throw her into other arms; she’s not looking for revenge. She’s looking for understanding, and, like her album title, she’s not afraid of feeling so much. Feeling too much is a tough path to take for women — or even men — in music. We’ve grown used to them heartbroken, vindictive or vindicated. But the steady supply of sadness, regret, pain and loss that Karol G dishes out in Me Arrepiento is not customary. To be clear, there is that one bichota, “female empowerment” track. “Matadora” gets very explicit in its description of a woman ready for non-romantic sex, and it’s also racking up streams. It’s the kind of club-banger that can propel an album. But this isn’t a banger album, and “Matadora” isn’t the biggest song from it so far. No Me Arrepiento is more defined by a slow burn of emotions, beautifully and painfully put into words. It’s a different kind of diva that Karol is giving us now — and audiences are showing that we like her, too. Your email address will not be published.

title: BMW R 1300 GS Adventure 10th Anniversary Edition Marks a Brazilian Milestone - stupidDOPE
content: A factory anniversary can easily become an exercise in commemorative badges and ceremonial paint. BMW Motorrad has taken a more considered route in Brazil, using the R 1300 GS Adventure to connect a decade of motorcycle production in Manaus with a significant manufacturing milestone. The resulting BMW R 1300 GS Adventure 10th Anniversary Edition is limited to just ten motorcycles, one representing each year of operation at the Brazilian facility. The choice of model carries particular weight. The R 1300 GS Adventure was also the 150,000th motorcycle produced at the Manaus plant, making the flagship adventure bike more than a convenient platform for a special edition. It represents both the scale BMW’s Brazilian operation has reached and the increasingly international manufacturing footprint behind one of motorcycling‘s most recognizable nameplates. Each anniversary motorcycle receives a deep olive-drab finish accented by yellow pinstriping and exclusive graphics across the fuel tank, side panels, and top case. An Akrapovič dual slip-on exhaust adds another distinguishing element, while BMW’s Automated Shift Assistant introduces a more consequential technological feature. The 1,300cc boxer engine remains mechanically unchanged, producing a claimed 145 horsepower and 110 pound-feet of torque. For a motorcycle already positioned near the top of BMW’s adventure range, the significance of this edition comes less from additional performance than from context. It connects an important motorcycle, a manufacturing landmark, and BMW Motorrad’s decade-long presence in Manaus through a production run small enough to function almost as a set of rolling historical markers. The tenth anniversary matters because BMW’s Manaus operation represents more than an assembly point serving a regional market. Reaching 150,000 motorcycles demonstrates sustained production at a meaningful scale, and selecting the R 1300 GS Adventure as the milestone machine connects that industrial achievement to one of BMW Motorrad’s most globally recognizable products. Brazil presents compelling reasons for localized motorcycle production. It is one of the world’s substantial motorcycle markets, with two-wheel transportation serving roles ranging from daily mobility to recreation and premium touring. Manaus, meanwhile, has long been an important manufacturing center through the Manaus Free Trade Zone, where industrial policy has encouraged domestic production across numerous sectors. BMW Motorrad’s presence there places the German company’s engineering culture within a distinctly Brazilian manufacturing context. That matters because modern premium vehicles are increasingly international products even when their brand identities remain closely tied to their countries of origin. The R 1300 GS Adventure captures that reality particularly well. Its engineering lineage is unmistakably BMW, from the boxer engine architecture to the chassis philosophy and electronics surrounding it. Yet this particular group of motorcycles also represents ten years of Brazilian production capability. The anniversary edition consequently commemorates people and infrastructure as much as machinery. Limited-edition motorcycles are common, but the logic behind their production numbers can sometimes feel arbitrary. A run of 500 or 1,000 examples creates scarcity, yet the number itself rarely contributes much to the story. BMW’s decision to produce ten examples is considerably more direct. One motorcycle represents each year of operation at the Manaus factory. That makes the limited quantity part of the commemorative concept rather than simply a mechanism for creating exclusivity. Numbering each example strengthens that connection. These motorcycles are not merely R 1300 GS Adventures equipped with an unusual paint package. Each occupies a specific place within a deliberately tiny production series linked to the facility’s history. That distinction will likely matter most over time. Special-edition motorcycles frequently become more interesting as the events they commemorate move further into the past. Production anniversaries, engineering transitions, final editions, competition victories, and factory milestones provide collectors with historical reference points that ordinary colorways cannot. The Manaus edition has two such anchors: the factory’s tenth anniversary and its 150,000th motorcycle. The deep olive-drab finish is particularly appropriate for the R 1300 GS Adventure. Adventure motorcycles already borrow some of their visual identity from expedition equipment. Large fuel tanks, exposed structural components, protective hardware, luggage systems, tall suspension, substantial windscreens, and upright ergonomics communicate purpose before the engine is even started. Olive drab pushes those associations toward military and field equipment without turning the motorcycle into a literal historical reference. Yellow pinstriping provides the necessary counterpoint. Against the muted bodywork, the brighter linework emphasizes the shape of the motorcycle while preventing the finish from becoming visually flat. Exclusive graphics across the tank and side panels establish the anniversary identity, while extending the treatment to the top case makes the luggage feel integrated into the design rather than attached afterward. Cases and other touring equipment occupy significant visual space, and mismatched accessories can disrupt an otherwise carefully developed design. Treating the top case as part of the commemorative package reinforces the sense that the edition was conceived as a complete motorcycle. The palette also avoids one of the more common problems with anniversary products: excessive decoration. BMW does not need gold surfaces, oversized dates, or elaborate graphics to communicate significance. The restrained finish suits a machine whose reputation was built around capability. The GS name carries unusual weight within BMW Motorrad. BMW’s adventure-bike lineage stretches back decades, and the GS family helped establish the template for large-displacement adventure motorcycles long before the segment became one of the industry’s most competitive categories. The formula combined long-distance road ability with off-pavement capability, upright ergonomics, luggage capacity, and the company’s horizontally opposed boxer engine. Modern GS models have become considerably more sophisticated, but that central proposition remains recognizable. The R 1300 GS generation represents a substantial evolution of the formula. Its 1,300cc boxer engine delivers 145 horsepower and 110 pound-feet of torque, output substantial enough to handle highway touring, luggage, passengers, steep grades, and off-road situations where careful throttle control becomes more important than outright power. The Adventure version expands the platform’s long-distance intent. That makes it particularly fitting as a factory milestone. A 150,000th motorcycle could have been almost any model on the production schedule. Having the number land on the R 1300 GS Adventure gives BMW a machine capable of representing the breadth of its modern engineering approach. It is technologically sophisticated, historically recognizable, and built for the kind of large-scale travel with which the GS identity has become synonymous. BMW has resisted the temptation to increase engine output simply to distinguish the anniversary edition. The familiar 1,300cc boxer remains rated at 145 horsepower and 110 pound-feet of torque. Special editions do not automatically become better when manufacturers increase power. On a large adventure motorcycle, additional output can have limited practical value compared with improvements in control, ergonomics, suspension behavior, heat management, reliability, or rider assistance. The existing engine already provides considerable performance. More importantly, the horizontally opposed twin remains fundamental to the GS experience. Its low-mounted cylinders contribute to the motorcycle’s recognizable silhouette while helping position substantial engine mass lower in the chassis. Decades of development have transformed the boxer from a historical curiosity into a highly sophisticated modern powerplant. Leaving it mechanically intact keeps the anniversary edition connected to the standard motorcycle rather than creating an unnecessarily altered derivative. BMW’s Automated Shift Assistant is arguably the anniversary edition’s most consequential equipment feature. The system replaces conventional manual clutch operation with electronic actuators capable of managing clutch and gear changes. Riders can retain control over shifting when desired or allow the motorcycle to handle gear selection automatically. That creates an interesting evolution for a category traditionally associated with mechanical rider involvement. Manual transmissions have long been treated as an essential part of motorcycling because clutch and gear selection contribute directly to the physical relationship between rider and machine. Automation inevitably raises questions about whether convenience removes part of that connection. BMW’s approach is more nuanced because it preserves choice. A rider can still select gears manually without managing a traditional clutch lever, while automatic operation becomes available when circumstances make it preferable. Heavy traffic, extended touring, fatigue, or repetitive low-speed riding can all make reduced clutch work attractive. Adventure motorcycles present a particularly interesting use case because their operating environments vary so dramatically. A rider might spend hours covering highway distance, navigate stop-and-go city traffic, climb winding mountain roads, and eventually encounter loose surfaces or technical terrain. A transmission system capable of changing behavior across those situations has legitimate value. Rather than simply making the R 1300 GS Adventure easier, the technology attempts to make it more adaptable. The Akrapovič dual slip-on exhaust provides a more traditional premium upgrade. Akrapovič has become deeply established within high-end motorcycle culture, with its exhaust systems appearing across everything from road-going sport bikes to racing machinery and adventure motorcycles. The brand’s reputation comes from a combination of materials expertise, weight reduction, acoustic tuning, performance development, and manufacturing quality. On the anniversary R 1300 GS Adventure, the dual slip-on configuration provides a visible distinction from standard equipment while complementing the motorcycle’s premium positioning. The exhaust also introduces another sensory element. Motorcycles are experienced through sound and vibration as much as visual design. An exhaust system can change the character of an otherwise familiar powertrain without requiring fundamental engine modifications. That makes the Akrapovič system a logical addition to a commemorative model whose engine output remains standard. It adds personality without disrupting the proven mechanical foundation. The R 1300 GS Adventure also illustrates how dramatically the adventure category has evolved. Early adventure motorcycles were comparatively simple machines whose appeal came partly from mechanical straightforwardness. Modern flagship ADV bikes increasingly resemble technological showcases, incorporating sophisticated electronics, electronically managed suspension, advanced braking systems, selectable riding modes, navigation integration, radar-based assistance on some models, and increasingly automated drivetrain functions. This evolution reflects what riders ask these motorcycles to do. A modern adventure bike may serve as a commuter, interstate touring machine, weekend canyon motorcycle, two-up traveler, gravel-road explorer, and long-distance expedition platform. That breadth requires compromises, but it also rewards adaptable technology. BMW’s Automated Shift Assistant belongs within that trajectory. Purists may prefer complete manual control, and simpler motorcycles retain advantages in cost, weight, familiarity, and field serviceability. Yet the growth of electronic assistance does not necessarily contradict adventure riding. Technology can reduce workload during mundane sections and preserve rider attention for situations that demand it. The anniversary edition therefore represents more than ten years of factory production. It also captures where the GS concept has arrived technologically. Perhaps the most interesting aspect of the R 1300 GS Adventure 10th Anniversary Edition is the geography behind it. BMW remains inseparable from German engineering culture, yet the Manaus edition demonstrates how international the production of premium vehicles has become. Manufacturing expertise does not remain confined to the location where a brand was founded. A Brazilian-built anniversary GS makes that reality visible. For the Manaus workforce, the 150,000-unit milestone represents accumulated manufacturing experience. For BMW, it demonstrates the ability to maintain a premium product identity across an international production network. For collectors, the ten motorcycles connect those industrial circumstances to a physical object. That gives the edition a kind of authenticity that cannot be created solely through cosmetic customization. The olive-drab paint, yellow pinstriping, numbered production, exclusive graphics, Akrapovič exhaust, and Automated Shift Assistant all contribute to desirability. Yet the motorcycle’s real distinction comes from what it represents. The best commemorative vehicles make their special status easy to explain decades later. The BMW R 1300 GS Adventure 10th Anniversary Edition already has that advantage. It celebrates ten years of production at BMW’s Manaus factory, arrives as a ten-unit numbered series, and uses the same model that became the facility’s 150,000th motorcycle. Its specifications reinforce the story without overwhelming it. The deep olive-drab finish and yellow pinstriping establish a distinct visual identity. The Akrapovič dual slip-on exhaust gives the motorcycle an appropriate premium hardware upgrade. Automated Shift Assistant demonstrates where BMW’s touring technology is heading. Meanwhile, the unchanged 145-horsepower boxer preserves the mechanical character of the underlying R 1300 GS Adventure. That balance is important. Anniversary models often become collections of options assembled around a commemorative badge. This edition has a clearer reason to exist because the motorcycle itself is directly tied to the event being celebrated. Only ten examples ensure that relatively few riders will ever own one, but scarcity is not the most interesting part of the project. The Manaus edition captures a specific moment in BMW Motorrad’s manufacturing history while demonstrating how far the GS has evolved from its comparatively elemental adventure-bike origins. FPS players need hair-trigger inputs for fast movement and aiming. Racers, meanwhile, are looking for finer control for steering and acceleration. As your skills improve, how you use your keyboard will change, too. Logitech G gaming keyboards are meant to be flexible. You don’t need to compromise on a keyboard that isn’t the right fit, because keyboards like the G 512 X and G 316 X are fully customizable to help you play your own way. Nobody can know what works for them straight away. It’s all about the fine-tuning. The Logitech G512 X has two actuation points to set how far you need to press a key before it registers, allowing one key to trigger one action with a light press and another on a full press. The included SAPP rings give you a tactile bump at that second point so you can feel exactly when it activates. The result is a board that gives you huge control over how quickly it responds. What about the layout? Logitech's G512 X 75 strips away the numpad and function keys. The G512 X 98 gives them all back. It’s the same core keyboard either way, but you get to choose how many keys you need and how much space it takes up on your desk. Customization doesn’t have to mean deep-diving into a long settings menu. The Logitech G316 X takes a simpler approach, putting everyday controls directly onto the keyboard. Its onboard dial and dot-matrix LED display let you quickly switch settings such as volume, media, and brightness, as well as your keyboard’s polling rate. Its mechanical switches are hot-swappable too, with customizable PBT keycaps that let you change the board's look and feel. Competitive players don’t settle. They’re always looking for tiny improvements to their game. Logitech G keyboards give you the space to step out of your comfort zone and try out new techniques. This is where the Logitech G512 X comes into its own. The G512 X has 39 dual-swap keys that let you switch between TMR (tunnel magnetoresistance) analog and traditional mechanical switches. TMR switches recognize how far you press a key, rather than just whether or not you’ve pressed it. A lighter press might let you ease around a corner while you’re racing, or push further when you want maximum acceleration. Analog input for your WASD keys adds precision to your gameplay, giving games a range of inputs. Here’s an example: You’re playing F1 2026, and you want to go — and go fast. With TMR analog switches, your acceleration isn’t just on or off; it’s zero to 100%, depending on how hard you press that W key. You can then use mechanical switches for abilities where a simple keypress works best. You’ve got the freedom to build your keyboard around the games you play, with functionality that doesn’t get in the way. You don't need to be a pro to get in on the action. The G316 X’s minimalist design and straightforward configuration give you a serious-looking setup without hours of unnecessarily complicated settings to wade through. Its gasket-mounted construction and sound-dampening layers shape how the keyboard feels and sounds, while configurable RGB lighting lets you customize the look. The same QWERTY keys might look identical, but individual game profiles mean they don't have to act the same way. Rather than rebuilding your controls each time, you can save your key preferences, shortcuts, and macros for each game, and the G Hub app loads your presets automatically when you launch. That leaves you with a choice: Which Logitech G keyboard is the one? The G316 X is beginner-friendly, with hot-swappable mechanical switches and onboard controls that are easy to master. The G512 X models are for players who want to get into the weeds, with adjustable actuation and much more control over how individual keys respond. Logitech designed these keyboards to let you play your way. Your keyboard isn’t set in stone. It’s something you can shape around your games, preferences, and playstyle. title: Karol G's 'Bby Wow' Hits No. 1 — And the Song It Dethroned Was Her Own - Latin Times
content: Karol G just did something almost nobody pulls off in Latin music: she took her own song down from the top spot. "Bby Wow," her team-up with Judeline and Rusowsky, vaulted from No. 5 to No. 1 on Billboard's Hot Latin Songs chart for the week of Aug. 29, edging out her own hit "Ahí" with Drake, which slides to No. 4. It's the Medellín singer's 11th trip to No. 1 on that chart, and it's a feat no act has managed against themselves in almost two years. For the two Spanish artists riding shotgun on the track, reaching No. 1 is a first-time milestone in more ways than one — "Bby Wow" also became their debut chart-topper on Billboard's Hot Latin Rhythm Songs list, where it likewise jumped from fifth to first, and Billboard flagged it as the top-ranked pairing involving a Latin act currently sitting on that particular list. Judeline, whose given name is Lara Fernández Castrelo, told Billboard she's still catching up to how quickly it all happened, saying it's "hard to believe a song we recorded last month is already topping the charts." Her fingerprints are on more than just that one song — she has writing credits on four tracks from the album altogether, a list that also includes "Matadora" (it entered at No. 4) and "Te Llevas To" (No. 6), both of which arrived on Hot Latin Songs the week before "Bby Wow" took over. The single's climb is one piece of a much bigger takeover. Karol G's sixth studio album, "No Me Arrepiento de Sentir Tanto," out since Aug. 7, marked her fifth trip to the top of Billboard's Top Latin Albums chart and is now holding that position for a second consecutive week. At the peak of its rollout, 13 different songs from the record crowded onto Hot Latin Songs in a single week — a stretch that also produced guest turns from Drake and Bruno Mars. "Bby Wow" pulled in 6.1 million official U.S. on-demand streams in its tracking week, per Luminate figures cited by Billboard, and reached as far as position No. 38 on Billboard's all-genre Hot 100 tally, Karol G's best showing there in two years. "Ahí" wasn't a slouch either: its debut brought in 11.8 million streams worldwide, good for No. 44 on the Hot 100 and a berth at No. 103 on the Global 200, while "Still," the record's collaboration with Bruno Mars, notched the set's strongest Hot 100 opening at No. 41. There's a live-show angle here that matters for two of the audiences this outlet covers most closely. Karol G's "Viajando Por El Mundo Tropitour" already got underway — she kicked things off with a pair of packed shows in Chicago back in late July — and the trek is now working its way toward Texas and Florida. It's set to stop at Houston's Reliant Stadium on Sept. 27 before landing at Miami Gardens' Hard Rock Stadium for two nights, Oct. 2 and Oct. 3, according to tour listings on Ticketmaster. For South Florida, the Hard Rock dates carry extra weight: it will be Karol G's first performance in the Miami market since August 2023, when she played the city on her "Mañana Será Bonito" tour, NBC 6 South Florida reported when the tour was first announced. Fans catching either stop this fall are likely to hear "Ahí" and "Bby Wow" fresh off their runs atop the Latin charts, alongside deeper cuts from a record that's currently dominating the genre almost on its own. What the past two chart weeks really show has less to do with any single track and more to do with how much ground Karol G is currently holding. "DTMF" no longer sits at No. 1, but it hasn't fallen out of the upper tier either — it's remained parked at No. 2 through the entire changeover. Karol G, meanwhile, has now spent back-to-back weeks running the very top of the chart with two different songs pulled from the same album. Not many acts have pulled off that particular trick: Bad Bunny is the only other recent example, back when his single "Nuevayol" gave way to his own "DTMF" as 2025 began. Among women, Karol G is the only one to have done it before — her own 2023 single "Qlona," featuring Peso Pluma, is what dethroned "Mi Ex Tenía Razón" that year. For scale, the longest No. 1 run of 2024 on this same chart was Karol G's own "Si Antes Te Hubiera Conocido," which lasted 14 weeks — a fraction of "DTMF's" 72-week hold. Whether "Bby Wow" can stay on top anywhere near that long is the question next week's chart data will start to answer. © {{Year}} Latin Times. All rights reserved. content:
When a high-flying fund crashes, the shockwaves can spill beyond its own balance sheet. Following a sharp mid-summer sell-off in the semiconductor sector, the artificial intelligence-focused hedge fund Situational Awareness sustained a devastating 67% portfolio drawdown. To meet escalating margin calls, the fund liquidated the bulk of its public equities at a steep discount. Now, regulators are asking hard questions about the institutions that bankrolled those trades. The Securities and Exchange Commission recently issued subpoenas to four major Wall Street prime brokers. Regulators want to understand the timing of the fund's trades, its communications with lenders, and how these banks monitored such aggressive leverage. While a regulatory inquiry of this magnitude might sound the alarm for a systemic banking sector crisis, a closer look at the underlying fundamentals tells a different story. The immediate threat does not lie in bank insolvency. The more relevant risk investors need to watch for is the potential for a forced, market-wide deleveraging cycle. To understand how the market is digesting this regulatory probe, it helps to look at the financial health of the prime brokers involved. The fundamental baseline for these institutions is incredibly strong, creating a meaningful buffer against immediate liquidity stress. During the most recent quarter, The Goldman Sachs Group NYSE: GS delivered a substantial earnings beat. Goldman Sachs topped consensus earnings per share estimates by over $6.50, while revenue rose nearly 40% year-over-year. Similarly, JPMorgan Chase & Co. NYSE: JPM beat consensus estimates by approximately 55 cents per share, backed by a revenue jump of around 27%. These are not institutions showing signs of immediate balance-sheet distress; they are generating billions in operating cash flow. Capital return programs also signal management confidence and provide a solid floor for equity valuations. Bank of America NYSE: BAC recently authorized an approximately $40 billion share repurchase program, which could retire up to 11% of its outstanding stock. Retiring shares reduces the overall float, ultimately boosting future earnings per share. Citigroup Inc. NYSE: C is actively executing an approximately $30 billion buyback plan of its own, targeting up to 13.7% of its shares. Market positioning reflects this fundamental stability. Short interest across all four of these banking giants remains at healthy, normalized levels. Institutional short-sellers are not aggressively betting against these equities, suggesting the broader market views the Situational Awareness collapse as an isolated incident rather than a systemic failure in prime brokerage. If the banks are fundamentally sound, the natural question is why the Securities and Exchange Commission is issuing subpoenas. The answer lies in the mechanics of margin lending and counterparty risk management. Prime brokers provide hedge funds with the capital needed to amplify their trades. In the case of Situational Awareness, the fund reportedly used heavy leverage, with some reports describing leverage near four times gross exposure. For every dollar of core capital, the fund borrowed roughly three dollars to maximize its exposure to the booming artificial intelligence (AI) trade. When the underlying semiconductor stocks reversed course, those amplified gains quickly turned into accelerated losses. The Securities and Exchange Commission is currently in a discovery phase, investigating how Wall Street facilitates and manages the risk profile of a single, highly concentrated fund. Regulators are scrutinizing internal risk-monitoring protocols to determine whether Goldman Sachs, JPMorgan Chase, Citigroup, and Bank of America took on excessive risk by maintaining such elevated leverage. They are also reportedly examining the efficacy and timing of the subsequent margin calls. When a leveraged fund experiences a severe drawdown, its prime broker issues margin calls requiring the fund to deposit additional cash or sell assets to cover the borrowed funds. If the fund cannot provide cash, it must liquidate holdings. In crowded sectors like semiconductors, forced selling can drive asset prices down further, triggering additional margin calls for other funds holding the same assets. The central issue is whether this extreme leverage points to a broader vulnerability in how prime brokers monitor clients. Regulators want to ensure that if a few heavily leveraged funds face sudden drawdowns, the resulting margin calls do not create localized liquidity vacuums or disrupt the broader financial system. The immediate downside risk to financial equities appears contained by their strong balance sheets, but the downstream risk to the broader market warrants careful attention. If the Securities and Exchange Commission uncovers systemic weaknesses in how Goldman Sachs, JPMorgan Chase, Citigroup, or Bank of America monitor client leverage, regulators could mandate stricter capital requirements or tighter oversight on margin lending. Even without a direct regulatory mandate, prime brokers might preemptively tighten their financing terms to avoid further scrutiny and mitigate their own counterparty risk. A credit-tightening cycle in the prime brokerage space creates ripple effects across the financial landscape. Hedge funds heavily reliant on borrowed capital would face higher margin requirements and reduced borrowing capacity. To meet these new constraints, funds would be forced to unwind positions and sell assets, draining liquidity from the market. This potential deleveraging event intersects with notable macroeconomic headwinds. The upcoming September Federal Open Market Committee meeting adds complexity. If interest rates remain elevated for longer than anticipated, the cost of carrying heavy leverage compounds. A scenario in which borrowing costs remain high while prime brokers simultaneously restrict access to margin could accelerate forced-liquidation pressure across the entire hedge fund sector. Wall Street's largest prime brokers possess the capital reserves and fundamental strength to weather this specific regulatory inquiry. The 67% wipeout was strictly due to Situational Awareness, not to the banking institutions that financed the trades. Regulatory spotlights alter institutional behavior. As prime brokers review their internal risk models and prepare to answer subpoenas, the availability of easy, cheap leverage may begin to shrink. When credit terms tighten, highly leveraged market participants are usually the first to feel the squeeze, often leading to sudden bursts of volatility in crowded trades. Investors may want to evaluate their portfolios for exposure to sectors favored by leveraged funds. Monitoring how JPMorgan Chase, Bank of America, Citigroup, and Goldman Sachs adjust their margin lending practices in the coming months can provide valuable clues about where broader market liquidity might tighten next. Capital preservation often depends on identifying structural shifts in market liquidity before they trigger widespread selling pressure. title: 2017 Lexus GS F For Sale With 89,900 Miles - AOL.com
content: The Lexus GS F is a rare and increasingly appreciated alternative to the German super-sedans, built around a glorious naturally aspirated V8 in an era of turbochargers. This 2017 example is finished in Ultra White over black and carries a strong service record. It is on Cars and Bids at $30,000 with six days to go and very active bidding. The GS F has held its value well, helped by its rarity and Lexus’s reliability reputation. According to Edmunds and current listings, clean examples generally trade from the mid $30,000s into the low $50,000s depending on mileage and condition, with a well-kept higher-mileage car appraising in the $40,000s, against a sticker near $84,000 when new. This car’s desirable naturally aspirated V8, strong maintenance record, and tasteful modifications support the range, while the higher mileage and the notes below temper it. At $30,000 with six days remaining and 39 bids in, the price should climb into the high $30,000s or low $40,000s. The car is a well-maintained, tastefully modified example. Finished in Ultra White over black, it runs the 5.0-liter naturally aspirated V8, rated at 467 horsepower with a 7,300-rpm redline, through an eight-speed automatic to a torque-vectoring differential, with adaptive suspension, heated and ventilated sport seats, a head-up display, and a Mark Levinson sound system. It has tasteful, reversible modifications including a Tanabe axle-back exhaust, an intake hose, an oil catch can, a strut tower brace, and wheel spacers, and importantly, the factory mufflers are included. A couple of points deserve attention. At 89,900 miles it is higher-mileage for the model, but the GS F is famously robust and the Carfax shows consistent, frequent oil changes, so the maintenance has been diligent. The seller reports about 25,000 miles on the current EBC brake pads with original rotors, and estimates pads, and likely rotors, will be needed within roughly 10,000 miles, so budget for that. There are also chips and scuffs on the front fascia. A pre-purchase inspection rounds it out. Rear wheel drive with torque-vectoring differential Interested in this 2017 Lexus GS F? View the listing here. The GS F was Lexus’s shot at the BMW M5 and Mercedes-AMG E63, and it took a deliberately different path. Rather than chase its rivals with turbocharging, Lexus fitted a naturally aspirated 5.0-liter V8 that revs to 7,300 rpm and delivers its 467 horsepower with a linearity and a howling top-end that forced-induction engines simply cannot replicate. Backing it are genuine performance credentials: a torque-vectoring differential, extra chassis bracing, adaptive suspension, and big Brembo brakes, all wrapped in a comfortable, beautifully built cabin with Lexus’s legendary reliability. That combination of a characterful, high-revving V8, real driving engagement, and famous dependability is exactly what makes the GS F so appealing, and increasingly collectible now that GS production has ended. It offers most of the thrills of the European super-sedans with a fraction of their maintenance anxiety, a genuinely rare and rewarding proposition. I have a real soft spot for the GS F, and this one hits the important notes. The naturally aspirated V8 is the star, a dying breed that sounds and revs like nothing with a turbocharger, and pairing it with Lexus reliability makes for a super-sedan you can actually use hard without dread. The tasteful, reversible modifications add a little voice without spoiling it, and the factory parts are included. Fair value sits in the $32,000 to $44,000 range, most likely around $36,000 to $40,000, reflecting the desirable engine and strong maintenance against the higher mileage and the upcoming brake service. Before bidding, get a pre-purchase inspection, budget for the brakes, and confirm the modifications suit you. Handle that, and you own one of the last great high-revving naturally aspirated super-sedans, with the reliability to drive it every day. Disclaimer: This post is for informational purposes only. title: New bodega bringing 1920s style to St. Cloud's East End - St. Cloud Times
content: A new 1920s-style convenience store is coming to St. Cloud's East End. Marla Waseka owns the building under MoXie Ladies, LLC and will operate St. G's Bodega with her two daughters. Bodega, a term commonly used in large, overcrowded cities, such as New York City, where space is at a premium, is similar to a small neighborhood convenience store. Waseka says she plans to keep the vibe of a 1920s-era grocery store atmosphere. The family-owned facility aims to have grab-and-go food with tables and chairs near the front windows. It will be located next door to The Kitchenette. “We will probably not have a cat, although we have had many inquiries since a neighborhood cat is a typical bodega element,” Waseka told the St. Cloud Times. The St. Cloud City Council approved the store's tobacco license on Aug. 17. Located at 415 E. St. Germain St., the arrival of St. G's Bodega currently is planned to time with the East Side’s annual Festi-Fall East that occurs Sept. 20. “This store is a puzzle piece that fits right into the rejuvenation concept of creating an urban, walkable entertainment district and definitely benefits the businesses we have next door,” Waseka wrote on Facebook earlier this summer. Earlier this summer, Waseka also bought the former Ace Bar building, which had been closed for a decade. She plans to renovate it and reopen it as a bar and restaurant at some point in the future.

title: Sena and BMW reveal co-developed intercom system ahead of 2026 GS Trophy - Visordown
content: Sena is set to become the official communication provider for riders, marshals and organisers of the 2026 BMW Motorrad International GS Trophy next month. Sena is set to provide 90 communication systems for riders, marshals and organisers of the 2026 BMW Motorrad International GS Trophy, which takes place from September 13-18, in Romania. The intercom specialist will act as an official partner of the race, with teams set to receive BMW ConnectedRide COM P1 GS and Sena 60X units throughout the event. But it’s not just competitors, marshals and the organisers that will benefit from this new partnership, as Sena’s Expand Mesh Multi-Sport headsets will allow photographers and videographers to stay in touch with teams. The new set-up focuses mainly on the BMW ConnectedRide COM P1 GS, with 55 units set to be provided. The system has been co-developed by Sena and BMW, and can be integrated into the new BMW GS Rallye Carbon helmet. To make group communication easier, the system uses Mesh Intercom and combines microphone noise reduction with second-generation HD speakers. As well as the 55 BMW ConnectedRide COM P1 GS, Sena will provide 25 60X systems which feature Mesh Intercom, Sound by Bose and a new joystick designed for use with gloves. Speaking about the new agreement with BMW, Vlada Bokza, European Motorcycle Marketing Manager at SENA, said: “It is at the heart of the action that we truly understand how our intercoms are used, what works perfectly and what we can still improve. The Int. GS Trophy 2026 puts us directly in contact with riders and their needs.” Finally, the company will throw in 10 Mesh Multi-Sport headsets, enabling members of the organisation that are travelling by car, including photographers and videographers, to stay in communication with teams on the ground without needing to wear a motorcycle helmet.
